gc5.design_note: The path guard flags ANY change to a forbidden zone anywhere in <B1-base>..<cut-C>, regardless of which track's commit made it. Empirically confirmed 2026-09-03: this interval contains 451 changed files, including 95 under frontend/ and genuine B2 additions under api-gateway/.../presence/ and modifications to ReadOnlyEnforcementFilter.java -- because B1 and B2 share the same trunk and merge window. A flagged forbidden-zone hit is therefore evidence requiring an explicit reviewed disposition (see reviewed_exceptions), not an automatic B1 violation and not something this tool may silently wave through -- 'the file was already on main' / 'that was B2, not B1' reasoning is exactly the loophole the review warns against auto-applying. Also empirically confirmed: B1's OWN commits (Wave 0 62237deb, Wave 4b cab2814e, Wave 5b 0b5d60d1) touched files under frontend/, but only under frontend/tests/**, frontend/pacts/**, and playwright.config.ts (e2e specs, pact contracts, test helpers) -- never frontend/src/** (production UI). That is why the allowlist below distinguishes frontend test/contract infrastructure from frontend/src/**, rather than exempting frontend/ wholesale.
gc5.always_allowed_globs_note: Test fixtures and workflow/doc files per tasks.md's path-guard description ('an explicit allowlist (test fixtures, workflow files)'). A match here is never itself a violation, but does NOT exempt a file from the content guard -- a forbidden symbol inside an allowed-path file (e.g. a *Test.java under portfolio-service referencing the presence module) must still be caught, per Task C's own negative-fixture requirement. Task 6 adds the exact policy path because a policy cannot embed its own future blob id; this is not a wildcard and does not exempt analyzer/runtime code.
